DP 606 · Rev. 01 · 16 Apr 2026

HR Projects Operations Procedure — Executive Summary

Prepared by HR Projects Procurement · Reviewed by HR Director, QM Director, Operations/QA Manager · Approved by CEO. Governs blue-collar sourcing, manpower market intelligence, manpower supplier management, project schemes, day-to-day HR Projects Operations, accommodation, catering, and project employee relations.

Objectives

3.1 — Ensure compliance with local labor laws, employment standards and regulatory requirements through proactive market research.
3.2 — Ensure the project deployment plan is aligned with execution strategies.
3.3 — Oversee all on-site HR operations: attendance, annual leave, travel and employee relations.
3.4 — Support onboarding and project-specific orientations/trainings.

Key Responsibilities (4.0)

HR Projects Operations Team — plans, executes and manages all HR functions for project staffing, pre-award through demobilization; secures labor-law compliance sources per country.
OD & Compensation/Benefits — align with Cost Control & Proposal on the deployment-plan gate review; PM leads handover and validates the plan with HR Projects Operations.
Procurement — evaluates commercial offers from suppliers/subcontractors; Cost Control prepares/assigns budget and reviews offers for alignment.
HR Projects Operations — accommodates employees, workers and visitors per the Accommodation Scheme.

HR Projects Operations Scope

Role Scope — Executive Summary

The HR Projects Operations role is built on 7 major task areas spanning market intelligence, advisory, project HR management, lifecycle administration, employee relations, data/reporting, and compliance — each carrying a defined weight of time and a matching KPI set.

Task Breakdown & KPIs

Reading the Scope — Observations

Heaviest load: HR Data Management & Reporting carries the largest weight (20%) — attendance/timesheet accuracy, payroll-support calculations and weekly reporting. This is also the most automatable task area (see the Monitoring tab for Power BI/Power Automate recommendations).
Three tasks tied at 15%: HR Advisory & Managers Support, Strong HR Project Management, and Onboarding & Offboarding, plus Policy Implementation & Compliance — together these represent 60% of time and are the tasks most exposed to labor-law and audit risk.
Lightest, highest-leverage tasks: Country & Project Survey and Benefits & Employee Relations are weighted at 10% each but sit upstream of major risk items in the Procedure's Risk Register (manpower delay, poor supplier quality, grievance backlog) — under-resourcing them can cascade into the heavier tasks.
Governance link: Task 3's KPI ("% Exceptions vs Applying the Project Scheme") and Task 7's KPI ("compliance with HR audits") map directly onto DP606's Process KPIs 3 and 10 — the two documents should be tracked together, which the Monitoring tab now does.

Task Assignment & Monitoring Cockpit

Assign a New Task

Eon Business Hub's matrix structure means many valid task owners never appear on the HR org chart. Fill in name & email here instead — it overrides the dropdown above and the task still tracks, links to its KPI, and emails the owner exactly like any other assignment.

✏️ Editing existing task: — submitting below updates this task in place (no duplicate created).

Clicking Assign task saves it to the board and immediately opens an email to the assignee (using the email address on file — populated from the Employee Roster Upload, the Org Chart tab, or the name/email typed above for matrix-org assignees) with the task, priority and due date pre-filled. If no email is on file yet, you'll be asked for one.

How to Assign & Monitor Tasks Well

1 · Set SMART tasksSpecific outcome, Measurable done-criteria, Achievable for the person's grade, Relevant to a KPI, Time-bound with a real due date — not "ASAP."
2 · Match task to person and loadCheck the workload bars below before assigning — a Team Leader already carrying 4+ open tasks is a risk, not spare capacity. Dual-site staff (flagged on the Org Chart tab) need extra headroom.
3 · Monitor outcomes, not activityReview status weekly against the board below rather than daily check-ins — daily pings read as micromanagement and slow people down without improving quality.
4 · Make "At Risk" safe to sayAsk assignees to move a task to At Risk themselves the moment they see a slip, and respond with support, not blame — that's what keeps the board honest.
5 · Close the loopWhen a task lands in Done, acknowledge it in the next 1:1 or team update. Recognition — even a one-line callout — is what sustains people updating status accurately over time.
6 · Escalate, don't absorbIf a task stalls because of a cross-functional blocker (Cost Control, Procurement, PM), route it through the Escalation Ladder on the Monitoring tab rather than quietly doing it yourself.

Labor Law Reference

Pick a country below, then type a term in the search box (e.g. “notice period”, “maternity”, “probation”, “transport”) or click one of the quick category buttons — search results are scoped to that country only, so what you see is exactly what applies where you're looking. Need to compare a term across markets instead? Switch to “All countries” next to the search box once you've typed something. This is a quick-reference summary of statutory employment terms for the markets where Eon Business Hub HR Projects Operations is active — a reference aid, not legal advice. Provisions change and interpretation varies by case, so always verify against the current official text and/or qualified local counsel before acting on anything shown here.

⚠ Local legal verification required. Labor law differs materially by country and changes over time. Every entry below was compiled from named public sources (official labour codes/acts where available, cross-checked against reputable secondary summaries). All 14 countries are aligned to the same structure — Attendance, Over Time, Leave Entitlement, Sick Leave, Maternity Leave, Compassionate Leave, Grounds for Termination, How to Calculate the Salary, Allowance's and Transportation, Casual Worker, and Probation Period — so any figure that couldn't be pinned to a firm statutory source is flagged in-line as needing local confirmation rather than guessed. Do not rely on any entry here as a substitute for confirmation from local legal counsel or the official gazetted text.

Cost of Living Reference

A country-level cost-of-living reference for the 15 markets where Eon Business Hub HR Projects Operations is active — useful for mobilization budgeting, expatriate allowance conversations, and sanity-checking a local compensation proposal. Pick a country below for its full breakdown, or leave "All countries" selected for the ranking view across every market.

⚠ Static snapshot, not a live feed. This page has no backend, so nothing pulls fresh numbers on its own — figures are refreshed manually on a quarterly (every 3 months) cadence, not daily or monthly. Data last compiled , next refresh due . Sourced from Numbeo's Cost of Living Index by Country (2026 Mid-Year edition, baseline New York City = 100) for the 11 countries it indexes at country level. Burkina Faso, Guinea Conakry, Sierra Leone and Sudan fall below Numbeo's minimum contributor threshold for a country-level index, so no index figure is published for them — their section below shows Numbeo's own raw sourced prices instead of a number Claude would otherwise have to calculate itself, each flagged with its contributor count so you can judge reliability. Always corroborate with a local cost-of-living survey or in-country HR contact before using any figure here in an actual compensation or allowance decision.
